messages:
Maya (CS): Hey team — Acme Corp flagged a month-end mismatch. Tableau export (our dashboard) shows 58,245,310 tokens for Nov; the invoice shows 61,704,122 tokens. They noticed it during month-close review. Can we triage?
Jamal (Support): Thanks Maya — can you paste the account id and the exact export CSV you used? Also did they use the dashboard UI export or our scheduled Tableau extract? :eyes: 
Maya (CS): Account: ACME-00412. They downloaded the scheduled Tableau extract (daily_extract_nov.csv) on 2025-12-01. I'm attaching the header snippet they sent: `account_id, date, plan_tier, tokens_used, embeddings_tokens` — totals aggregated per day.
Priya (Billing): FYI invoices are generated from the metering pipeline (metering-service -> ingestion -> billing-agg) and include all token categories (prompt, completion, system, embeddings). Metering also de-dupes by request_id and attributes tokens to the plan that was active at the request timestamp. There is a ~24h ingestion lag for late events.
Lucas (DataEng): Possible culprits: 1) Tableau extract query is joining to the app logs (which can include retries) without de-duping request_id, 2) plan-tier attribution mismatch if plan changed mid-month, 3) timezone/truncation causing a day boundary shift. Can you confirm if ACME had a plan change in Nov?
Maya (CS): They upgraded from Starter -> Pro on 2025-11-20 15:42:03 UTC. They called that out as a potential cause — dashboard shows tokens under "Pro" for Nov 1-30, but invoice breaks out pre/post upgrade.
Jamal (Support): Can we run a quick cross-check query? Something like:
```
SELECT r.request_id, r.timestamp, r.account_id, r.plan_at_time, r.tokens_total, m.tokens_total AS metered_tokens
FROM app.requests r
LEFT JOIN metering.events m ON r.request_id = m.request_id
WHERE r.account_id = 'ACME-00412' AND r.timestamp BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2025-11-30';
```
Look for duplicated request_id or NULLs on m.request_id.
Lucas (DataEng): Running that now on prod-backfill. Early spot check: found ~1,120 rows where app.requests has duplicate request_id (retries logged) and metering.events has single entry. Tableau extract was summing app.requests.tokens_total without DISTINCT on request_id — that explains lower dashboard number (duplicates dropped? wait, duplicates would inflate dashboard). Actually the dashboard export uses the materialized view `dashboard.daily_usage` which was joining on request_id incorrectly and used `COUNT(*)` in a subquery for retries. I'm seeing duplication patterns and also ~3,500 events that arrived after 2025-12-01 ingestion cutoff (so invoice included them later).
Priya (Billing): So invoice is higher (61.7M) because it includes late-arriving events and system tokens that the Tableau extract wasn't summing?
Lucas (DataEng): Exactly. Two things: (A) Tableau extract logic omitted system tokens and embeddings in that specific export (bug in ETL config), (B) late-arriving metering events were ingested into billing pipeline before invoice generation cutoff, so invoice reflects them. The net delta from these two explains ~3.45M tokens.
Maya (CS): ACME is asking if invoice will be adjusted or if dashboard will be updated to match. They attached a csv diff.
Priya (Billing): Policy: we don't retroactively change invoices for late ingestion unless it's >1% variance and customer requests review. This delta is ~6% for ACME — borderline. I'll open a billing review ticket but need a reproducible delta breakdown.
Jamal (Support): Action items: Lucas to produce a day-by-day reconciliation table (metering vs dashboard extract) with counts for prompt/completion/system/embeddings and highlight late-arriving events; Maya to share the exact CSV from ACME; Priya to hold invoice adjustments pending reconciliation.
Lucas (DataEng): Will do. Quick repro SQL I'll run and share a delta CSV by EOD:
```
WITH deduped AS (
  SELECT request_id, MAX(timestamp) as ts, SUM(tokens) as tokens, MAX(plan_at_time) as plan
  FROM app.request_events
  GROUP BY request_id
)
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, plan, SUM(tokens) as dashboard_tokens, SUM(m.tokens_total) as metering_tokens, COUNT(*) as rows
FROM deduped d
LEFT JOIN metering.events m USING (request_id)
WHERE d.account_id = 'ACME-00412' AND ts BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2025-11-30'
GROUP BY day, plan
ORDER BY day;
```
Lucas (DataEng): Preliminary numbers look like: dashboard_total=58,245,310, metering_total_invoiced=61,704,122, late_arrivals=3,421,010, system_tokens_excluded_from_export=37,800. I'll attach the CSV to the ticket.
Maya (CS): ACME: "We need an explanation and whether we can get a credit if this was caused by your export bug." They're upset but calm.
Priya (Billing): Once Lucas posts the CSV I'll run the formal variance calc and open a billing-review. If variance >1% and trace shows ETL omission, we'll offer a partial credit and update the dashboard pipeline to match billing semantics going forward.
Jamal (Support): Note for runbook: update Tableau ETL to use `metering.final_usage_view` instead of `dashboard.daily_usage` and ensure de-dupe on request_id and include columns for system and embeddings tokens.
Maya (CS): Thanks. tagging ACME contact copied into ticket. :+1:
billing-bot: Created ticket BLG-2025-438 for billing-review, assigned to Priya.
Lucas (DataEng): Uploaded reconciliation CSV to BLG-2025-438 and pushed a fix to the ETL repo: `fix/tableau-include-system-tokens` (PR queued).
Priya (Billing): I'll wait for the reconciled CSV then propose next steps. Thanks everyone.
Maya (CS): I'll keep ACME updated and escalate if they push for immediate credit. 
Jamal (Support): Closing loop later today after Lucas' CSV. :thumbsup:
